 West Palm Beach, Fla (CBS12) — A blustery and unsettled pattern is expected across the Treasure Coast and Palm Beaches this week, with strong northeast winds, rounds of coastal showers and dangerous beach conditions. 
 Continued northeasterly flow will continue to push scattered showers and a few storms into the picture throughout the beginning of the week. (WPEC) 
 Occasional gusts will still have the potential to be as high as 35-40 miles per hour, especially in coastal areas. (WPEC) 
 The biggest concerns will be coastal flooding around high tide, rough surf, beach erosion and hazardous boating conditions. 
 Some improvement is expected later in the week, though showers and coastal hazards may linger. 
 Windy with showers to start the week 
 Northeast winds will remain gusty Monday, with the strongest winds near the coast. 
 Coastal areas could see sustained winds around 20 to 25 mph, with frequent gusts of 30 to 35 mph and isolated gusts possibly reaching 40 to 50 mph in showers. 
 Sustained winds of 20-25 miles per hour will be present, along with occasional gusts up to 35-40 miles per hour. (WPEC) 
 The Treasure Coast has the better chance for showers Tuesday, while rain chances taper farther north and west. 
 Highs will generally be in the low to mid 80s. 
 Coastal flooding and dangerous beach conditions 
 High tides will bring the potential for significant saltwater flooding along the coast in the coming days. 
 High tide times will be between 9 and 10 a.m. and 9 and 10 p.m. the next two days. (WPEC) 
 Strong onshore winds and large surf could push water onto low-lying roads, lots and properties, while also causing beach erosion. 
 Major coastal flooding is possible during high tide cycles over the next couple of days; coastal flooding may continue later in the week, especially where rain falls in vulnerable areas. 
 Coastal flooding will continue to be present, mainly near high tide times, through Wednesday. (WPEC) 
 Avoid driving through flooded roads. 
 Beach and boating conditions will also be hazardous. 
 A high risk of rip currents and a High Surf Advisory are in effect, with breaking waves of 7 to 13 feet forecast in the surf zone. 
 Dangerous rip currents can be expected through late Wednesday night. (WPEC) 
 Large breaking waves will continue to be present courtesy of gusty northeasterly winds. (WPEC) 
 Dangerous surf is expected along the Palm Beaches, and entering the ocean is not advised. 
 Gale conditions and very rough seas are forecast offshore, with hazardous marine conditions expected through at least midweek.
 Strong winds will create hazards for boaters in offshore waters. (WPEC) 
 Showers linger; winds ease later in the week 
 As the week progresses, winds should gradually ease, but showers and a few thunderstorms remain possible each day.
 Any downpours that continue to move over the same spots can result in an isolated flood risk until Thursday morning.
 An isolated risk of flash flooding will exist from a few training downpours in some spots through the first half of the work week. (WPEC) 
 Rain chances look highest Wednesday and Thursday, particularly from Cape Canaveral southward. 
 Later in the week, showers may be more favored inland as winds turn northeast to east-northeast. 
 High temperatures should stay in the low to mid 80s, with overnight lows mainly in the upper 60s to low 70s. 
 Even as winds and seas slowly improve toward the end of the week, high tides and coastal showers could keep flooding concerns around. 
 Check the latest local advisories before heading to the beach or going out on the water.
